scope: Personal PC education branch Toss quote/history/display coordination; no broker orders or live AI calls
symptoms: New US-wide strategy accounts remain waiting for data or cannot obtain execution quotes.
403 responses were indiscriminately reported as a server IP block.

findings.problem: Independent Toss clients issue mutually revoking OAuth tokens.
findings.evidence: Official FAQ specifies one valid access token per client and immediate predecessor revocation. Separate quote, history and display clients previously issued independently.
findings.resolution: Personal local mode shares an encrypted token, serialized by a cross-process file lock. An in-flight rejected token adopts an already-published successor before issuing again.

findings.problem: All HTTP 403 responses were classified as IP allowlist failures before parsing the error envelope.
findings.evidence: OAuth access_denied indicates an IP denial, while edge-blocked and generic forbidden responses are distinct; invalid_client is authentication failure.
findings.resolution: Parse bounded JSON first; separate explicit IP, edge, permission and authentication errors. Show static safe reasons through isolated workers and the dashboard.

findings.problem: History fallback could hide edge/permission failures.
findings.resolution: Propagate provider-wide denials to retry status without a Yahoo fan-out. Retain Yahoo fallback for symbol-specific missing or invalid history.

full_suite.environment: Isolated temporary runtime and Python 3.14 venv; no user runtime or real credentials used

coverage: Rotated secret cannot read old cache or overwrite new token after failed authentication
History and paper child preserve safe provider reason
No Yahoo fan-out on provider-wide denial
No plaintext client credentials or bearer in encrypted cache

direct_review.functionality: One-client one-token coordination spans issuance and atomic publication; request retries are bounded to one; history progress and ledger behavior retained.
direct_review.performance: Cache reads and token lock are bounded; one issuance for 30 queries from three spawned roles. No repeated large catalog or full backup introduced by this change.
direct_review.code_quality: Existing platform file lock and bounded I/O helpers reused; read-only endpoint allowlist retained; git diff --check passed.
direct_review.security: AES-GCM cache key is derived from the client secret and context; private token directory/files; no plaintext credentials or tokens in archives, logs or status; runtime OAuth cache excluded from backups; cloud/production credential custody unchanged.

operating_notes: Stop the running native launcher, update the existing folder, and restart.
No strategy or paper-account recreation is required.
After client key reissue, save the latest Client ID and Client Secret together.
The shared cache coordinates a single installation. Other PCs, independent folders or external applications issuing tokens for the same Client ID can still revoke it.
A genuine allowlist mismatch still requires registering the executing PC's public IP in Toss WTS.
Full-market initial history preparation must complete before fresh selection. Quote freshness, corporate actions, strategy filters and trading-session gates still apply.
limitations: No live Toss credentials were used; the reported remote installer account has not been directly observed.
The reproduction enforces the documented token rule on a local HTTP server; it is not a real brokerage endurance run.
This fixes evidenced common defects and improves diagnosis; it does not establish that every reported remote failure has the same cause.
